control_implications.headline: NetScaler ADC patches address authentication bypass
control_implications.significance: An authentication bypass in widely deployed NetScaler ADC could allow unauthorized access to critical infrastructure. The vulnerability management owner should confirm patch deployment across all NetScaler instances and verify compensating controls where patching is delayed.

control_implications.headline: ConnectWise ScreenConnect deployments enable MSP attack paths
control_implications.significance: Exploitation of a patched ScreenConnect flaw indicates persistent supply chain risk through managed service providers. The third-party risk owner should review MSP access scopes and request evidence of vulnerability remediation from all ScreenConnect suppliers.

control_implications.evidence_excerpt: Most organizations haven't sorted out their cryptographic estate enough to even know where they'd start with post-quantum cryptography (PQC).
control_implications.headline: Cryptographic estate unprepared for post-quantum cryptography
control_implications.significance: Lack of cryptographic inventory undermines governance oversight for post-quantum migration. The governance owner should assign accountability for cryptographic asset discovery and record a risk decision on migration timeline.

paragraphs.text: Critical vulnerabilities in Citrix NetScaler, Apache HTTP Server, and N-able N-central are being actively exploited, while credential theft campaigns compromise thousands of GitHub accounts and ScreenConnect deployments enable MSP supply chain attacks. These developments demand urgent vulnerability remediation, privileged access review, and third-party assurance validation across affected infrastructure.

Most organizations lack visibility into their cryptographic estate, leaving them unprepared for post-quantum cryptography migration. Control owners should initiate cryptographic inventory efforts and confirm governance ownership for long-term cryptographic risk decisions.
